result.title: OmniGround: Strengthening Omni-Modal Temporal Grounding via Attention-Consistency Training
result.summary: Omni-modal large language models can jointly understand video, audio, and text, yet they remain weak at temporal grounding, a capability essential for real-world audio-visual applications. To understand this limitation, we look beyond final predictions and examine the model's internal temporal evidence. We identify a temporal generation gap: the internal attention of the model localizes the target moment more accurately than the timestamps it generates. To close this gap, we propose TACG (Temporal Attention-Consistency Grounding), a post-training method that treats internal attention as a reliable temporal pivot and aligns it with both the model prediction and the ground-truth annotation through attention-consistency training. We further build a 580K-sample training dataset by reconstructing temporal QA from dense audio-visual annotations and organizing general omni-modal instruction data. Using TACG and this training dataset, we train OmniGround, a general-purpose omni-modal model with stronger temporal grounding capability, without injecting any additional temporal cues. OmniGround reaches state-of-the-art omni-modal temporal grounding, including 37.5 mIoU on LongVALE and 35.7 mIoU on UnAV-100, while staying competitive on both general audio-visual understanding and vision-only grounding.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对全模态模型时序定位薄弱的问题，发现「内部注意力比生成时间戳更准」的时序生成鸿沟，提出 TACG 后训练方法，用注意力一致性训练把内部注意力与模型预测、真值标注对齐，并构建 58 万样本数据训练出 OmniGround 模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其内部状态比显式输出更可靠的诊断，与 LVR 关心的隐状态信息是否被答案使用、监督与贡献分配问题相通；把注意力当作枢轴做一致性对齐的训练思路，可供核查是否能用于对齐 latent 推理状态与最终答案。
